storyboard.claim: The teenagers have power only because the armband grants it, and they answer to no moral code.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smirking young man in a grey hoodie beside the law icon: a boy holding authority he did not earn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the high school enforcers point from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The law icon shows authority handed down; the smirk shows the thrill of it, not a civic duty.

storyboard.claim: The host questions whether the dome itself changed Big Jim, which is a question about sequence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim pondering with a clock icon: the timeline is what is being tested.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the debate about whether the dome created Big Jim's behaviour.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock reads as time and sequence; Jim is the figure whose timeline is in question.

storyboard.claim: Did the sealed-in isolation of the dome break Big Jim's mind and make him a megalomaniac?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim under the drawn dome: the isolation the host is asking about.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the timeline challenge; now names the dome's isolation as the suspected cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dome icon anchors the question in the sealed town; the thinking pose keeps it a question, not a verdict.

storyboard.claim: The host says the question needs a different reading, which is a distinction about sociology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim in thought with the callout carrying the claim: a reframing, not a fact.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from the question to the answer the hosts are building.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon fits a reframing; the callout carries the beat.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim was already running a massive methamphetamine lab before the dome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim smirking behind the mask icon: a respectable public face hiding a criminal enterprise.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the timeline question: the criminal empire predates the dome.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask reads as a false public face, which is the literal point of a town leader hiding a lab.

storyboard.claim: Jim hoarded propane, stole money and trafficked narcotics: a criminal empire under the town's nose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim with the coin icon: cash taken from the town, the crime made literal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the crimes that already existed before the dome fell.
storyboard.addedInformation: The coin reads as cash on hand, which is literal here: stolen money, not a metaphor about money.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the idea that the dome drove Jim insane: he was always a tyrant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim with a hard angry face under the dome icon; the strike rejects the dome as the cause.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the dome-as-cause theory raised by the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the rejected phrase; the angry face carries the tyrant claim.

storyboard.claim: The dome removed the DEA, IRS and attorney general, giving Jim impunity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim smirking beside the law icon: the outside law that would have checked him is gone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the dome did: removed outside law, not character.
storyboard.addedInformation: The law icon reads the missing authority; the smirk reads the freedom it gives him.

storyboard.claim: The dome is a catalyst: it accelerates rot already hidden in the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: the dome, hidden rot, accelerated.
storyboard.onScreenText: The dome makes the rot spread
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the answer into the pressure-cooker model the hosts use.
storyboard.addedInformation: A flow diagram shows the cause and effect structure without relying on a metaphor the viewer must decode.

storyboard.claim: Pressure cooker ingredients get hotter and more concentrated until they break down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Heat icon with Jim in thought: the pressure building under the surface.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the pressure-cooker analogy from the flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire reads as heat here, which is the literal mechanism of a pressure cooker.

storyboard.claim: An authoritarian needs a scapegoat to blame for the pressure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie in the cell, thinking about being blamed; the callout names the need for a scapegoat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from the pressure model to the people who take the blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads scapegoat literally without a risk of misreading; the callout carries it.

storyboard.claim: Barbie is a drifter, an Iraq war veteran and a short-order cook, sitting on his bunk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie seated on the cell bunk beside the war icon: his combat past.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Barbie in the cell.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon reads the literal military past; the sad seated pose sets the grim scene.

storyboard.claim: A confession was forced from Barbie for murders he did not commit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie holding a cup of water in the cell: the drink the police gave him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the forced confession and the glass of water.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cup is the object he handles; the callout carries the forced confession, since no icon reads it literally.

storyboard.claim: The police salted Barbie's drinking water: petty cruelty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie with the cup and an angry face: the salt taste made visible through his reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the water beat with the cruelty of the salt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry face is the reaction to cruelty, not a generic emotion; the cup ties the callout to the water.

callout.text: Town leadership isn't just framing him

storyboard.claim: Barbie realises the town leadership is not merely framing him but torturing him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie thinking with the puppeteer icon: one group controlling his fate.
storyboard.onScreenText: Town leadership isn't just framing him
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the salted water: from the cruelty to the realisation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer reads as one person controlling others, the leadership pulling the strings.

callout.text: Salting the earth of his life

storyboard.claim: The town leaders are salting the earth of Barbie's life as psychological torture; scapegoating is the mechanism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim angrily pointing at Barbie in the cell: the accuser and the accused.
storyboard.onScreenText: Salting the earth of his life
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the realisation into the accusation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point and angry face stage the accusation; the callout carries the salt metaphor the viewer cannot read alone.

storyboard.claim: When society panics, people look for a target rather than the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia with her notes beside the target icon: a panicked town picking a victim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Barbie's cell to the general mechanism of panic.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target reads as aiming at a victim; the notes show the truth the panic ignores.

callout.text: The easiest scapegoat is the outsider

storyboard.claim: The outsider is the easiest scapegoat in a closed system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie thinking in the street: the outsider the town chooses.
storyboard.onScreenText: The easiest scapegoat is the outsider
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the target idea to Barbie specifically.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads outsider literally; the callout carries the claim.

storyboard.claim: Barbie has no roots in town, and he has already clashed with Big Jim's son.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie thinking with Junior beside him: the outsider and the son he already fought with.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reasons Barbie fits the scapegoat role.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads transient; the callout carries it. Junior is staged as the clash partner, not in a fight.

storyboard.claim: Societal panic needs a focal point to burn off anxiety, and Big Jim uses an outsider.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim smirking in the street: the manipulator who knows the focal point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the scapegoat mechanism through Big Jim.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk is the sinister charm of a man who uses the crowd, not a friendly face.

callout.text: Whips the citizens into a frenzy

storyboard.claim: Big Jim whips the citizens into a frenzy from the town hall steps.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim angrily speaking with the puppeteer icon: one man controlling the crowd.
storyboard.onScreenText: Whips the citizens into a frenzy
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the manipulation of the crowd in the speech.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer reads one person controlling others; the angry talk reads the threat of the speech.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim brands Barbie a terrorist and says he murdered the town's women.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim pointing at Barbie: the accusation delivered to the crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the content of the speech.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point stages the accusation; the word terrorist has no icon and rides on the callout.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim's own son actually committed the murders Big Jim blames on Barbie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Junior with a sinister smirk: the real killer the town never looks at.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the irony behind the accusation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk is the guilt of the real killer, not friendly warmth.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim takes Mrs. McCain's grief over her murdered daughter and turns it against Barbie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim pointing with the grave icon: a murdered daughter's grief redirected.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the manipulation of the grieving mother.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave reads the death behind the grief; the angry point reads Jim turning it into a weapon.

storyboard.claim: The raw trauma is aimed at Barbie like a laser, a masterclass in manipulation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie with a fearful face in the street: the trauma aimed at him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes what the grief becomes once it is aimed at Barbie.
storyboard.addedInformation: Afraid is the fear of the target; surprised would read as wow, not fear.

storyboard.claim: The hosts must critically examine Barbie's own role in his downfall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie thinking in the cell: the self-examination the hosts are about to make.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from Jim's manipulation to Barbie's own part.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads self-examination; the callout and the thinking pose carry it.

storyboard.claim: Barbie's avoidance was a flawed strategy: Colonel Cox begged him to take military command.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie beside the war icon: the military command he refused to take.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the mistake Barbie made early on.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon ties the refused command to the military past; the callout names the flaw.

storyboard.claim: Colonel Cox ordered Barbie over the phone; the president authorised the command and Barbie refused.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie holding a phone: the call from the outside that he turned down.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the specific moment of the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone is held as an object, not a phone icon, so the viewer does not read a smartphone anxiety.

callout.text: Just be the short order cook

storyboard.claim: Barbie wanted to be only the short-order cook and stay out of it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie in the diner beside the food icon: the cook he wanted to remain.
storyboard.onScreenText: Just be the short order cook
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why he refused the command.
storyboard.addedInformation: The food icon reads a dinner plate for the cook's job; the callout carries the reason for his avoidance.

callout.text: Federal military authority as an outsider

storyboard.claim: Asserting federal military authority as an outsider in a paranoid town would have got him killed faster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie thinking with the hosts' challenge: the outsider's authority in a hostile town.
storyboard.onScreenText: Federal military authority as an outsider
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host pushes back on the critique of Barbie.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads federal authority; the callout carries the argument.

callout.text: Martial law commander of Chester's Mill

storyboard.claim: Imagining Barbie declaring himself martial law commander on the car hood, which the thugs would have answered with violence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie pointing from the street with the law icon: the self-declared command in the hypothetical.
storyboard.onScreenText: Martial law commander of Chester's Mill
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the hypothetical concrete: what a public declaration would have meant.
storyboard.addedInformation: The law icon reads the martial law claim literally; neutral keeps the speech a hypothetical, not a fact.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim's thugs would have shot Barbie in an alley and claimed he resisted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie sprawled on the street with eyes shut: the hypothetical killing the callout names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Finishes the hypothetical with the outcome.
storyboard.addedInformation: Collapsed reads fallen; afraid shows the fear before it happens. The callout keeps it a conditional.

storyboard.claim: Laying low was tactical survival, not moral abdication.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie beside the shield icon: protection, survival instinct.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defends Barbie's avoidance as survival.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads protection, the literal meaning of survival; the negation is carried by the callout.

storyboard.claim: Laying low still abdicated the moral responsibility the moment required.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie slumped in the cell: the duty he gave up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The counter-argument to the survival defence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump plus sad reads the cost of his failure; no icon reads moral duty literally.

storyboard.claim: By the time Barbie realises he must act, it is too late; the narrative is hijacked by Rennie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie slumped beside the clock: time has run out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the consequence of the delay.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock reads deadline; the slump reads defeat, not a generic tiredness.

storyboard.claim: The scapegoat machinery is fully operational and Barbie is strapped to the altar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie with a fearful face beside the chains icon: bound and offered up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the fate the delay produced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read bound and controlled, which is literal here; the altar is carried by the callout.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the idea that the dome created the town's willingness to hate; it only boiled it up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia thinking under the dome icon; the strike marks the rejected idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the core thesis: the dome is a catalyst, not the origin.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the dome as origin; the thinking pose is the argument, not a verdict.

callout.text: Cooked it to a boiling point

storyboard.claim: The dome did not invent the town's hatred, it cooked it to a boiling point.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia talking in the office: the pressure-cooker claim in words.
storyboard.onScreenText: Cooked it to a boiling point
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the pressure-cooker model as the conclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads the boiling point literally without repeating fire; the callout carries it.

storyboard.claim: A fascist takeover needs more than a tyrant and a scapegoat; it needs an audience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim with an angry face: the tyrant the claim refers to.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the audience idea by first naming the tyrant.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry reads the threat of the tyrant, not a friendly face; the audience is named in the callout.

storyboard.claim: The audience needs fuel, the most unsettling people in Chester's Mill.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim with a sinister smirk in the street: the people who fuel the takeover, set up for the next beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Points to the next group of people the hosts will discuss.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: no icon reads fuel literally without repeating fire; the callout carries the claim.
